gen_risks.description: High dependence on Official Development Assistance and low domestic revenue mobilization create fiscal volatility that could impact project sustainability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize grant-based IDA financing for full project funding and lock in multi-year resource commitments within the Project Operations Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: Persistently low domestic revenue mobilization has kept STP heavily dependent on Official Development Assistance (ODA), leaving fiscal revenues highly volatile.

gen_risks.description: Recurrent extreme climate events such as floods and coastal storms may damage infrastructure, disrupt electricity, and delay service delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt climate-resilient EDGE design standards for center construction, procure backup power generators, and include a Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC).
gen_risks.evidence: STP is vulnerable to coastal and riparian floods, severe storms... may cause disruptions in service delivery, potentially leading to short delays.

gen_risks.description: Cross-ministerial coordination complexities across MLSSS, MECSHE, MEYST, and MAFRD may cause delays in annual workplan preparation and execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a Strategic Coordination Committee under the Minister of Labor and formalize inter-institutional roles in the Project Operations Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: delays in preparing annual workplans and implementing interventions due to the involvement of multiple stakeholders

gen_risks.description: Fiduciary management bottlenecks within AFAP, including delayed transaction recording and internal audit backlogs, could hinder project implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Designate a dedicated project accountant, customize the financial accounting software, and expand external audit scope within six months of effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: delays in recording financial transactions... internal audit reviews not conducted in a timely manner, leading to identification of weak controls

gen_risks.description: Non-compliance with selection criteria or payment processing issues could delay grant and stipend disbursements to vulnerable youth and MSMEs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Define objective eligibility criteria in the POM, leverage the Unique Social Registry, and execute direct transfers via a contracted electronic Payment Service Provider.
gen_risks.evidence: delays in availing funds for beneficiaries resulting from possible non-compliance in selection criteria.

gen_risks.description: Social exclusion or elite capture in selecting beneficiaries for scholarships, sub-grants, and internships could prevent marginalized youth from participating.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use objective socio-economic data from the Unique Social Registry, mandate a minimum 50% quota for women, and maintain an active Grievance Redress Mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: risks of exclusion, which may arise if project benefits are not equitably distributed... risks of elite capture in the selection of beneficiaries

gen_risks.description: Risks of sexual exploitation, abuse, and sexual harassment (SEA/SH) during training sessions or employer workplace placements, particularly affecting young women.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire a dedicated Social/GBV Specialist within 45 days of effectiveness, integrate SEA/SH prevention codes into institutional agreements, and establish confidential reporting channels.
gen_risks.evidence: community health and safety risks, including risks of sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and sexual harassment (SH), particularly for young women

gen_risks.description: Sub-grants to micro-enterprises in agriculture, fisheries, or tourism might cause localized environmental degradation or pollution if improperly managed.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require environmental risk screening for all sub-grant proposals and train business incubators and MSMEs on ESG standards and sustainable practices.
gen_risks.evidence: small business grants could support micro-enterprises... that may indirectly place pressure on sensitive ecosystems or cause localized pollution

gen_risks.description: Geographic isolation, transport constraints, and high material supply costs on Príncipe Island could cause construction cost overruns and timeline delays for the new training center.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct early site-specific engineering assessments, centralize procurement through AFAP, and build realistic cost buffers into the procurement plan.
gen_risks.evidence: Príncipe—home to just about 10,000 people—is more than 170 km away and experiences compounded isolation.

gen_risks.description: Existing public TVET institutions suffer from outdated equipment, staff gaps, and weak industry linkages, threatening training quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide direct financing for modern equipment procurement, instructor upskilling, and establish Workforce Development Committees with private sector employers.
gen_risks.evidence: capacity remains constrained by outdated equipment, limited infrastructure, insufficient operating budgets, staffing gaps, and weak employer participation

gen_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity and fragmented existing tools at DTEFP could impede the operationalization of the new labor market information system.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit specialized technical consultants, provide targeted staff training, and modernize DTEFP office equipment and cloud-based architecture.
gen_risks.evidence: Services for labor intermediation... remain at an early stage of development... tools and processes... are currently fragmented, underutilized, and poorly interconnected.

gen_risks.description: Delays in hiring key environmental, social, TVET, and IT specialists within legal covenants timelines could stall initial project implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Initiate early drafting of terms of reference and leverage the existing restructured SPRRP Project Implementation Unit team to maintain momentum.
gen_risks.evidence: hire or appoint, not later than forty-five (45) days after Effectiveness: (i) one Environmental Specialist... (ii) one Social Specialist

gen_risks.description: STP's small, highly informal private sector may lack sufficient absorption capacity to hire trained youth in wage employment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Combine wage employment support with self-employment starter packages, MSME productivity growth grants, and labor mobility orientation.
gen_risks.evidence: Micro and small enterprises make up 92 percent of all firms... Most are household-run and provide few job opportunities.

gen_risks.description: High desire among youth to emigrate may result in skilled graduate flight without yielding economic returns to the local domestic economy.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate structured labor mobility frameworks (such as Global Skill Partnerships) and pre-departure guidance to maximize remittance flows and formal overseas placement.
gen_risks.evidence: 68 percent of youth are considering leaving the country in search of better opportunities abroad... emigration has yielded limited economic benefits

gen_risks.description: Unreliable power supply and grid failures could disrupt digital operations, cloud databases, and the online Employability Portal.
gen_risks.mitigation: Procure backup power generators for DTEFP and deploy cloud-based software architectures with offline-capable data synchronization capabilities.
gen_risks.evidence: Structural constraints such as costly and unreliable electricity... intense rainfall and floods which may disrupt electricity access

gen_risks.description: Interagency bottlenecks between technical teams at MLSSS and fiduciary specialists at AFAP could slow contract drafting and evaluation processes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear procurement workflows in the Project Operations Manual and mandate joint bi-weekly progress reviews between MLSSS and AFAP.
gen_risks.evidence: A key factor for good procurement performance will be the ability of AFAP and the MLSSS to work in close collaboration

gt_risks.description: Frequent government changes and the cross-ministerial nature of the jobs agenda can shift policy direction, counterpart arrangements, and implementation momentum; further changes may follow the mid-2026 legislative/parliamentary elections. Success depends on sustained coordination across labor, education, tourism, agriculture, and finance ministries plus private-sector engagement.
gt_risks.mitigation: Anchor the project within MLSSS (core employment-promotion mandate); strengthen technical ownership at directorate level rather than relying on political leadership; establish a formal coordination committee and a unified PIU; continue policy dialogue with Government during implementation.

gt_risks.description: STP's fragile growth outlook, narrow fiscal space, and dependence on external financing leave it highly vulnerable to external shocks (energy/food price swings, donor-disbursement delays, climate events), which may weaken labor demand, reduce firms' absorption capacity, and constrain the Government's ability to sustain recurrent-cost interventions (training, stipends, employment services).
gt_risks.mitigation: Prioritize low-cost, scalable interventions; combine supply-side investments with direct job-creation support; target sectors with growth potential and external demand linkages (incl. labor mobility); coordinate with other World Bank macro-fiscal/energy/private-sector engagements in STP.

gt_risks.description: Limited experience of MLSSS and DTEFP in delivering complex labor-market interventions at scale; fragmented institutional landscape; multiple implementation partners; nascent capacity in labor-market analytics, employment intermediation, and cross-sectoral coordination; sustainability risk if new systems/programs are not institutionalized within government structures and budgets.
gt_risks.mitigation: Leverage existing institutions/mechanisms rather than parallel structures (existing MLSSS PIU, coordination committee, AFAP for fiduciary/safeguards); finance targeted TA and staffing; invest in durable institutional assets (labor-market information system, employability portal, strengthened training institutions, formalized service-provider arrangements); use the learning agenda and impact evaluation to identify cost-effective interventions for scale-up.

gt_risks.description: Complex procurement in a small-island context: residual FM risk is moderate but residual procurement risk is substantial, driven by the complexity of civil works in a remote island context, the large number of technical-assistance contracts, and the multiplicity of projects already handled by AFAP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Agree ToRs and technical specifications between AFAP and the World Bank before initiating any procurement (prior and post-review); reinforce AFAP procurement and contract-management capacity incl. specialized support for civil-works supervision; embed dedicated fiduciary controls for the grants/stipends payment mechanism in the Project Operations Manual; continue and adapt the risk assessment during implementation.
